messages:
maria: Quick question ahead of tonight's handoff — can someone clarify the ownership boundary between SRE and runtime for alerts? The runbook mixes infra vs model problems and it's tripping up new oncallers.

jason: Short version: SRE = infra (nodes, networking, disk, k8s control plane, cluster autoscaler). Runtime = model-serving layer (model loads, KV cache, runtime process crashes, inference errors). If the issue is clearly infra (OOM on node, PV lost) page SRE. If it's model-specific (decoder hangs, KV cache thrash, sudden regressions in token generation) page runtime.

olivia: Can we put that in a 1‑paragraph blurb in the runbook? New folks keep paging the wrong team. Also propose an escalation pattern for cross-cutting problems.

jason: Agreed. Proposed escalation flow (suggested text for runbook):
```
1) Triage: determine if errors are coming from infra metrics (node/host-level) or serving logs (model runtime stack).
2) If infra -> page SRE primary (pagerduty-sre). If runtime -> page Runtime primary (pagerduty-runtime).
3) If both show severe degradation or source unclear -> page BOTH and label incident as SEV2 until ownership is resolved.
4) For total outage (all regions down or >80% request failures) -> SEV1, page oncall-leads + execs per incident playbook.
```
kevin: Leaving a handoff note: I'll be on-call until 03:00 UTC. Running a model-v2 canary on dedicated pool starting 00:30 UTC (low traffic). Expect sporadic latency spikes if the canary hits warmup. If you see increased 95p latency but only in canary pool, that should be runtime to handle.

maria: Thanks, kevin — I'll add that to the handoff template. One more thing: what's the definition of "incident" we should use for oncall notification thresholds? Some folks are treating any 5m spike as SEV.

jason: Good call. Proposed thresholds (add to runbook):
- SEV1: Service unavailable or >80% error rate across traffic for >5 minutes OR critical data loss.
- SEV2: Significant degradation (10–80% error rate or >=2x baseline latency p95) sustained >15 minutes or affecting core customers.
- SEV3: Small, localized issues, single-region, or transient spikes <15 minutes — handle in normal oncall flow, document in handoff notes.

olivia: I'm OK with those. I'll update the runbook and add the 1-paragraph ownership blurb and escalation snippet. Can someone from runtime (jason or kevin) approve the wording before I push?

jason: I'll review in ~15m. quick ack now: +1 to thresholds.

oncall-bot: Reminder posted: don't forget to add handoff context (canaries, ongoing rollouts, known flaps) to the ticket. :bell:

maria: Awesome — thanks all. This should reduce wrong-team pages. I'll include a short checklist at top of tomorrow's handoff doc: 1) current canaries 2) active deploys 3) expected maintenance windows 4) ownership quick-reference.

kevin: Added my canary details to the handoff doc (link: https://docs.internal/redwood/oncall/handoffs). Ping me if you want me to stay longer during the canary window.

maria: End of thread — summary will be copied into the runbook after jason's review. :white_check_mark:
